newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to see Reno, expected to retain her.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to see Reno, expected to retain her.

text.p: President Clinton was to meet with Attorney General Janet Reno Thursday or Friday to discuss her job status, and a senior administration official said Clinton was likely to ask Reno to stay on.
Reno was cautious at a news conference Thursday when asked whether she would remain at the Justice Department. "Anything like that the president has to talk about," she said.
Asked if the time had come for a decision on her future, she said: "You would have to ask them."

Questions about Reno's job security have arisen because of her independent streak, which has rankled the White House at times. Some Clinton aides have also complained that she has been too quick to succumb to Republican pressure for probes of administration officials by independent counsels.

But a source familiar with the president's thinking said he would be "very surprised" if Clinton did not ask Reno to remain in the Cabinet. The official said the press of other business had kept Clinton from meeting with Reno sooner.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton had spoken to Reno by telephone on the eve of her maiden oral argument before the U.S. Supreme Court on Wednesday and that they had a good conversation. He said they would meet Thursday or Friday.
Reno told reporters she would be at a White House dinner Thursday night and would meet Clinton earlier in the day as part of a group involved in a drug policy conference.
